question: Why is the thermal conversion of H2B-SiH2 to Si (μ-H2) BH2 not feasible, and what makes the reverse reaction more feasible?
answer: The thermal conversion of H2B-SiH2 to Si (μ-H2) BH2 is not feasible because it requires overcoming two high energetic barriers. In contrast, the reverse reaction from Si (μ-H2) BH2 to H2B-SiH2 is more feasible as it effectively requires overcoming only one barrier.

The purpose of the paper is to investigate the detailed reaction mechanism for the transformation of B and SiH4 into silicon tetrahydroborate (Si (μ-H2) BH2) using density functional theory (DFT) and high-level ab initio calculations. It aims to clarify the thermal and photochemical pathways involved, with particular focus on the energy barriers and the role of conical intersections (CIs) in the photochemical reaction. The study also seeks to explain experimental observations through computational insights into the excited-state characteristics and reaction coordinates.
